name: NY-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+32 partisan lean makes a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely
Open seat after Espaillat lost renomination, but the Democratic nominee starts with a huge structural advantage
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 97% to win
Republican candidate has reported no fundraising or outside spending
model.rationale: The D+32 fundamentals dominate everything else: even with Espaillat off the ballot and heavy outside spending in the Democratic primary, the general election pits a well-funded Democratic nominee against a Republican with no visible fundraising in a deep-blue Manhattan/Bronx district. Markets agree, pricing the Democratic side near 97%.
model.watch: Any sign of a fractured Democratic field or a credible independent challenge could widen the uncertainty, but the district's partisan baseline leaves little room for an upset.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Adriano Espaillat (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
NY-13 is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+32. Adriano Espaillat lost renomination, so the seat is open, but the Democratic nominee, Darializa Avila Chevalier, inherits the district's overwhelming structural advantage. She raised over $1.3 million and drew substantial outside spending in what was effectively the decisive primary contest.

The Republican nominee, Jomo Williams, reports no fundraising or outside support. Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee at roughly 97% to win. With no public polling and no expert ratings available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold in the mid-to-high twenties.
